newsitem.title: UK: BAe urges tough line on Airbus - paper.
newsitem.headline: BAe urges tough line on Airbus - paper.

text.p: British Aerospace Plc's chief executive Dick Evans has briefed Trade and Industry Minister Margaret Beckett and pressed her "to take a tough line" at a crucial meeting of the ministers from the four Airbus partners next week, a newspaper reported.

The Independent said on Friday that talks at the Paris airshow on progress towards turning the aircraft consortium into a commercial firm would be held amid concerns the French partner, St Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, was dubious about the transition.

BAe wants Beckett to seek assurances that that Airbus remains on track to become a fully commercial entity in 1999, the newspaper said, amid fears that France's new left-wing government may give more weight to the views of Aerospatiale in decisions about the consortium's future.

The chairman of Aerospatiale, Yves Michot, said last month that if BAe and the German partner Daimler Aerospace teamed up to take control of French defence electronics group Thomson-CSF, it would signal a "death warrant" for Airbus.

Michot also threw the future shape of Airbus into question last week by saying the Airbus partners had agreed that Airbus would have "management mandates" over factories and design centres but would not own them.
